summary: The design addresses a real upstream drop, but its session-store contract is not yet wired to the repository’s long-lived toolkit instances or multi-worker deployment model. The largest gaps are request isolation, durable handle ownership, the query-plus-upload handler path, and unresolved Jira size semantics.

suggestions.title: Make file resolution request-scoped, not mutable toolkit state
suggestions.rationale: `AbstractBot.session()` binds a task-local `RequestContext` containing `session_id`, while `FileManagerToolkit` and `JiraToolkit` are constructed as reusable instances. Mutating a toolkit’s root or handle map per request would let concurrent sessions overwrite each other. Introduce an injected session resolver or immutable per-request view, and reject attachment calls without a bound session.

suggestions.title: Persist the handle manifest and define worker-storage requirements
suggestions.rationale: `OUTPUT_DIR` is a filesystem path and the current file manager has no handle registry. An in-memory `file_id`→path map would disappear on restart and fail when upload and attachment requests land on different gunicorn workers, even though the design promises persistent session files. Store ownership metadata atomically beside the file or require a shared storage backend; test restart and cross-worker resolution.

suggestions.title: Do not reuse the current path resolver as the security boundary
suggestions.rationale: `FileManagerToolkit._resolve_output_path()` accepts absolute paths and uses a lexical `startswith` check. That is insufficient for traversal, sibling-prefix paths, and symlink escapes. Handle resolution must canonicalize the candidate, enforce containment under the session root, reject or safely handle symlinks, and sanitize stored filenames before any Jira I/O.

suggestions.title: Add explicit staging APIs for remote and generated files
suggestions.rationale: The existing `FileManagerToolkit` selects one backend at construction; `download_file()` downloads from that backend to a local destination, while `upload_file()` accepts a raw local source path. This does not by itself implement “remote source → local session store,” nor does it safely register an agent-generated artifact without exposing its path to the model. Define an explicit trusted staging/import operation that returns a handle, with Jira consuming only the resolver.

suggestions.title: Persist attachments before the query-handling branch
suggestions.rationale: `_handle_attachments()` calls `handle_files()` only when the request has no query. The query path enters streaming or non-streaming agent execution without passing the uploaded attachments into that persistence step. A multipart request containing both a file and a prompt can therefore still lose the file. Persist first, then dispatch the prompt, and add a regression test for that request shape.

suggestions.title: Define the Jira size limit as deployment configuration
suggestions.rationale: The installed `jira` client only detects an empty attachment after upload; the repository contains no Jira attachment-size limit configuration. Cloud and Server/DC limits differ, so a hard-coded 10 MB pre-flight rule cannot be correct until the open deployment question is resolved. Add an explicit per-tool or per-deployment byte limit, or document a bounded discovery mechanism, and test the configured boundary.

suggestions.title: Freeze one typed result envelope and attachment cardinality
suggestions.rationale: `jira_add_attachment` currently accepts one path and returns a top-level success object, while `jira_add_comment` accepts a list and returns an issue object with ad hoc attachment dictionaries. The proposed “same shape” and “one entry per input handle” are ambiguous for the singular tool. Specify whether both tools accept `file_ids: list[str]`, define Pydantic result models with stable error codes, and update callers and tests together.

suggestions.title: Specify partial-commit semantics for comments
suggestions.rationale: The current comment implementation creates the Jira comment before uploading attachments. If the comment succeeds and an attachment fails, the operation is already partially committed; preflighting the issue does not make it atomic. Return independent comment and attachment statuses, define whether attachment preflight occurs before comment creation, and test comment-success/attachment-failure explicitly.

suggestions.title: Expand tests beyond path-based Jira mocks
suggestions.rationale: The existing Jira attachment tests exercise local filesystem paths and the CSV agent test exercises only DataFrame registration. They do not verify non-tabular persistence, tabular persistence plus attachment, duplicate filenames, disk-write failure, multipart-plus-query uploads, cross-session handles, traversal, or restart behavior. These cases are required to falsify the new contract rather than preserve the old path loop.

suggestions.title: Bound and sanitize Jira error details returned to the model
suggestions.rationale: The intent says to surface Jira status and body verbatim, but response bodies can be large HTML documents or contain operational details and secrets. The current code has no normalized error contract. Preserve status and a bounded, sanitized diagnostic with a stable retry classification such as `forbidden`, `too_large`, or `transport_error`.

suggestions.title: Add aggregate session quotas and an operator cleanup contract
suggestions.rationale: `FileManagerToolkit.max_file_size` is a per-file limit, while the design deliberately keeps files until manual cleanup. Nothing currently bounds total bytes per session or provides a cleanup operation/runbook. Without an aggregate quota and ownership-aware cleanup, repeated uploads can exhaust `OUTPUT_DIR` even when every individual file is valid.

suggestions.title: Resolve the MIME decision before implementation and remove contradictory acceptance criteria
suggestions.rationale: The accepted brief simultaneously reverses the real-Content-Type requirement and still specifies MIME-aware multipart upload, `aiohttp`, and Jira endpoint posting. The installed Jira client hard-codes `application/octet-stream`. Either keep the locked simpler `jira.add_attachment` path and make MIME metadata advisory, or reopen the decision with a concrete Jira deployment test; do not leave both behaviors in the implementation contract.
